subject.title: [Feature]: Memory indexing lacks checkpoint/resume capability for long-running operations

question: What durable checkpoint/resume design should builtin memory-core use for interrupted full reindexes?
rationale: The source-proven gap is real, but the permanent fix changes persisted memory-index state, search/status semantics during incomplete generations, and possibly public config defaults, which are maintainer product/API choices.

options.title: SQLite-backed resume state
options.body: Persist generation/progress metadata in the memory-owned SQLite schema, resume compatible interrupted shadow builds, and keep search/status on the last complete generation until publish succeeds.

options.title: Retry and cleanup only
options.body: Keep the current atomic full-rebuild model and limit this issue to better retry, stale-shadow cleanup, and status diagnostics, accepting that process death restarts from zero.

options.title: Require explicit config design first
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers decide whether checkpoint intervals or resume behavior should become public `memorySearch` configuration.

recommendation.title: SQLite-backed resume state
recommendation.body: Persist generation/progress metadata in the memory-owned SQLite schema, resume compatible interrupted shadow builds, and keep search/status on the last complete generation until publish succeeds.

likelyOwner.reason: The safe reindex and atomic-helper history makes steipete the strongest routing candidate for the design tradeoff.
